Linert Contact Us Contact Advertise Submit News Statement of Values Terms of Service Public Notices Browse notices Place a notice Latest News Poland school board reviews reductions in district revenue By JT Whitehouse September 26, 2026 3 min read Trending POLAND -- School finances dominated conversation at this week's Poland Board of Education meeting. Last year, the district did not know what to expect because of legislation changes. This year, officials know that revenue will be flat. The 20-mill floor is one area affecting revenue. The 20-mill floor was enacted in 1977 to ensure a minimum level of funding for school districts in Ohio. In 2025, legislation made some changes to what counts toward the 20-mill floor that took Poland and some other districts off it, meaning the district could no longer benefit from increased property values. "Before the recent legislation, when property values rose, Poland would see an increase in revenue," Poland Local Schools Treasurer Jeanette Medina said. "Now, when property values go up, the tax (revenue) for Poland schools stays flat." Another area affecting the districts in Mahoning County is the recently approved owner-occupied housing credits. This credit came from Ohio HB 96, which allowed county budget commissions to double the Homestead exemption and/or the owner-occupied credits. At the state level, the Homestead Exemption credit was geared to giving retirees on fixed incomes a break. The retirees got the break and the schools did not lose anything as the state gave the schools the funds they had lost from the credit. Medina said when the county voted to double the owner-occupied credit, unlike the state, the county does not make up the difference to the school districts. The additional taxpayer discount ends up being a loss to school districts. The loss for the Poland district will be approximately $350,000 per year. "My big concern is the fluctuation in revenue," board member Greg Riddle said. Riddle pointed to the last few months and a concern about school finances. Because of all the legislation passed this year and the revaluation of properties, county auditors had to wait to see how to collect tax bills. Those invoices were due to be collected starting July 24, but because of the changes, the invoices were put on hold. The state did away with the penalty for late filing of property taxes for the mid-year collection. When the numbers were known, the calculations were done and the tax invoices were mailed and collecting began this month. "We got our first payment of half a million," Medina said. "By now we would normally see close to $8 million. We are still in the process of getting those funds. Thankfully we have enough money in our reserves to meet our obligations." Riddle added there are low-interest loans and possibly grants for energy efficiency improvements available from HB 15. He suggested having audits done of all the schools. The high school recently had one completed ,and the data it revealed will be released soon. Riddle said McKinley school could use new windows, and a roof on North might qualify as well. In other business at the meeting, donations were accepted for the Poland High School Interact Club, with $50 donations coming from Bodine and Co., Certus Health, the Hadi Chammas family, Sentinel Financial Services and Hooked Window Cleaning. Nolfi and Associates Insurance and Financial Services LLC donated $100 to the club. Starting at /week. Subscribe Today

https://english.republika.mk/macedonia/u.text: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will arrive to Skopje on Friday as part of her tour of the Western Balkans. According to her office, von der Leyen will hold meetings with President Gordana Siljanovska-Davkova and Prime Minister Hristijan Mickoski. Discussions will focus on the European prospects of Macedonia and the region, as well as the EU accession process. The issue regarding Bulgaria and potential ways to resolve it are also expected to be addressed. Ahead of von der Leyen’s visit, Foreign Minister Timcho Mucunski stated that Macedonia seeks a solution with Bulgaria that would ensure predictability in the European integration process. He noted a willingness among European institutions and certain EU member states to help strengthen mutual engagement and open avenues for discussion; however, he emphasized that the country’s position remains absolutely clear: under current circumstances, there are no conditions for constitutional amendments, given Bulgaria’s stance. Although bilateral contacts with Sofia have taken place, they have not yet yielded progress; consequently, according to Mucunski, assistance is needed from the interested party—the EU. Therefore, he views the upcoming visit to Skopje by European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen—during which this topic will be discussed in greater detail, among other things—in a positive light. There is no doubt in our country that a solution is needed, the minister says, but we are drawing a red line: the solution found must ensure predictability and security. The EC President will begin her tour of the Western Balkans on September 30 in Albania, followed by visits to Kosovo and Montenegro. This time, Serbia and Bosnia and Herzegovina will not be part of her itinerary. European Commission spokesperson Arianna Podesta announced that the two countries were excluded because they are preparing for elections. Serbia is set to hold early parliamentary elections on October 25, while general elections in Bosnia and Herzegovina are scheduled for October 4. The visit follows reports that the EU wants to create some form of EU accession that will not be blocked by vetoes from individual member states, but apply it only to Ukraine, Moldova, Montenegro and Albania. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cq8e.text: Image source, Anadolu via Getty Images Image caption, Syrian officials said five people were killed in the Jordanian strike on a village in the southern Daraa province By Toby Mann Published 28 minutes ago Jordan has struck what its military says were "terrorist organisations" in Syria in retaliation for an attack on a Christian funeral last week that killed nine people. Syrian health officials told state media five people, including women, children and an elderly man, were killed in the strike on a village in the southern Daraa province. Jordan said its fighter jets had killed and wounded "several terrorists", without giving further details. Jordan said it had co-ordinated with the Syrian government. Syria said it had not been notified of Monday's attack. It comes after a nine people were killed and 34 injured in a shooting at a funeral in a Greek Orthodox church in Karak on Friday. Figure caption, Watch: CCTV footage appears to show gunmen near church In response to the strike, Syria said it had closed a border crossing with Jordan. "The decision includes the complete suspension of passenger and commercial traffic in both directions, to ensure the safety of travellers and workers at the crossing," Syrian authorities said in a statement carried by state media. It added that it had "opened direct channels of communication" with Jordanian officials and had launched "comprehensive investigations to establish the full circumstances of the targeting". Nassib is the only passenger and commercial border crossing between Jordan and Syria. Earlier on Monday, senior government security officials said Jordanian security forces had arrested two brothers and their brother-in-law over the church attack. The Public Security Directorate (PSD) said the unnamed "terrorists" were found hiding in an abandoned house in Karak before dawn. Jordan's Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya told state-affiliated TV the attackers were all Jordanians and "had been holed up in a building in one of the villages near the site of the attack".
